parent: Verifying Whether Wholesome Roots Are Genuine or False

zh: 一、則相驗知者，即有二意：一、邪；二、正。邪者，如根本禪中諸觸發時，隨發一觸，若有邪法，即是邪相。邪法眾多，今約一觸中略出十雙邪法，以明邪相：一者、觸體增減；二、定亂；三、空有；四、明闇；五、憂喜；六、苦樂；七、善惡；八、愚智；九、縛脫；十、心強軟。此十雙明邪相，皆約若過、若不及中分別。
en: As for mark-verification, this has two parts: the deviant, and the correct. As for the deviant: when, within the root dhyānas, the various tactile sensations arise, whichever single sensation arises, if a deviant dharma is present within it, this is precisely a deviant mark. Deviant dharmas are manifold; here, with reference to a single tactile sensation, ten pairs of deviant dharmas are given in brief, to clarify the deviant marks: excess or deficiency in the sensation itself; concentration or agitation; emptiness or existence; brightness or darkness; sorrow or joy; pain or pleasure; wholesome or unwholesome; foolishness or cleverness; bondage or liberation; and a mind too rigid or too soft. These ten pairs, clarifying the deviant marks, are each distinguished in terms of excess on the one hand or insufficiency on the other.

zh: 一、觸體增減者：如動觸發時，或身動手起脚亦隨，然外人見其兀兀如睡，或如著鬼，身手紛動，或坐時見諸異境，此為增相。減者，動初發時，若上若下，未及遍身，即便漸漸滅壞，因此都失境界，坐時蕭索，無法持身，此為減相。二、定亂：定者，動觸發時，識心及身為定所縛，不得自在，或復因此便入邪定，乃至七日不出。亂者，動觸發時，心意撩亂，攀緣不住。三者、空有：空者，觸發之時，都不見身，謂證空定。有者，觸發之時，覺身堅䩕，猶如木石。四、明闇：明者，觸發之時，見外種種光色，乃至日月星辰青、黃、赤、白種種光明。闇者，觸發之時，身心闇瞑，如入暗室。
en: First, excess or deficiency in the sensation itself: as when, for instance, the tactile sensation of movement arises — the body moves, the hands rise, and the feet follow along, yet an onlooker sees the practitioner slumped as though asleep, or as though possessed, the body and hands moving about in disorder, or, while sitting, one sees various strange states — this is the mark of excess. As for deficiency: when the sensation of movement first arises, whether upward or downward, before it has spread through the whole body it gradually dissolves and collapses, so that the state is lost entirely, and while sitting one feels desolate and empty, unable to sustain the body at all — this is the mark of deficiency.

Second, concentration or agitation: as for concentration, when the sensation of movement arises, consciousness and the body become bound by the concentration itself, no longer free, and, through this, one may even fall into a deviant concentration, failing to emerge even after seven days. As for agitation: when the sensation of movement arises, the mind and intention become disturbed and disordered, chasing after one thing after another without ever settling.

Third, emptiness or existence: as for emptiness, when the sensation arises, one no longer sees the body at all, taking this to be the realization of an emptiness-concentration. As for existence: when the sensation arises, one feels the body hard and rigid, just like wood or stone.

Fourth, brightness or darkness: as for brightness, when the sensation arises, one sees various external lights and colors, even the sun, moon, and stars, and lights of blue, yellow, red, and white. As for darkness: when the sensation arises, body and mind grow dim and dark, as though entering a darkened room.

zh: 五、憂喜：憂者，觸發之時，其心熱惱，憔悴不悅。喜者，觸發之時，心大慶悅，勇動不能自安。六、苦樂：苦者，觸發之時，身心處處痛惱。樂者，觸發之時，甚大快樂，貪著纏綿。七、善惡：善者，觸發之時，念外散善覺觀，破壞三昧。惡者，觸發之時，即無慚無愧等諸惡心生。八、愚智：愚者，觸發之時，心識愚惑，迷惛顛倒。智者，觸發之時，利使知見心生邪覺，破壞三昧。九、縛脫：縛者，觸發之時，五蓋及諸煩惱覆蔽心識。脫者，觸發之時，謂證空、無相定，得道得果，斷結解脫，生增上慢。十、心強軟：強者，觸發之時，其心剛強，出入不得自在，猶如瓦石，難可迴變，不順善道。軟者，觸發之時，心志軟弱，易可敗壞，猶若軟泥，不堪為器。如是等二十種惡觸擾亂坐心，破壞禪定，令心邪僻，是為邪定發相。
en: Fifth, sorrow or joy: as for sorrow, when the sensation arises, the mind grows feverish and distressed, haggard and unhappy. As for joy: when the sensation arises, the mind is greatly delighted, stirred and unable to settle.

Sixth, pain or pleasure: as for pain, when the sensation arises, body and mind ache and suffer everywhere. As for pleasure: when the sensation arises, one feels an intense delight, craving and clinging to it without end.

Seventh, wholesome or unwholesome: as for the wholesome, when the sensation arises, the mind thinks of external, scattered wholesome discursive thought, breaking the samādhi apart. As for the unwholesome: when the sensation arises, states of mind such as shamelessness and lack of conscience, and other unwholesome minds, arise at once.

Eighth, foolishness or cleverness: as for foolishness, when the sensation arises, the mind and consciousness grow foolish and confused, deluded, dull, and inverted. As for cleverness: when the sensation arises, sharp discursive views arise in the mind as deviant cleverness, breaking the samādhi apart.

Ninth, bondage or liberation: as for bondage, when the sensation arises, the five hindrances and other afflictions cover over and obscure the mind and consciousness. As for liberation: when the sensation arises, one supposes oneself to have realized the concentration of emptiness or signlessness, to have attained the path and its fruit, severed the fetters, and become liberated — giving rise to overweening pride.

Tenth, a mind too rigid or too soft: as for rigidity, when the sensation arises, the mind becomes hard and unyielding, unable to move freely in or out, just like a tile or a stone, difficult to turn or change, and unresponsive to the wholesome path. As for softness: when the sensation arises, the will of the mind becomes weak and yielding, easily broken down, just like soft mud, unfit to be shaped into any vessel.

Such twenty kinds of unwholesome tactile sensations as these disturb the sitting mind, break dhyāna-concentration apart, and cause the mind to become deviant — this is the mark of a deviant concentration arising.

zh: 復次，二十邪法隨有所發，若不別邪偽，心生愛著者，因或失心狂逸，或歌或哭，或笑或啼，或時驚狂漫走，或時得病，或時致死，或時自欲投巖赴火，自絞自害，如是障惱非一。復次，二十種邪中，隨有發一邪法，若與九十六種道鬼神法，一鬼神法相應，而不覺識者，即念彼道，行彼法，於所得法中，鬼神隨念便入。因是證鬼神法門，鬼加其勢力，或發諸深邪定，及智慧辯才，知世吉凶，神通奇異，現希有事，感動眾生，廣行邪化，或大作惡，破人善根，或雖作善，而所行偽雜。
en: Furthermore: whenever any of these twenty deviant dharmas arises, if one fails to distinguish it as deviant and false, and the mind grows attached and clinging to it, this may cause one to lose one's mind and run wild — singing or wailing, laughing or weeping, at times startled and running madly about, at times falling ill, at times even dying, at times wishing to throw oneself from a cliff or into a fire, or to strangle or otherwise injure oneself. Such hindrances and afflictions as these are not of one kind only.

Furthermore: among these twenty deviant dharmas, whenever any single one of them arises, if it happens to correspond with any one of the spirit-practices of the ninety-six paths, and one fails to recognize this, then, in thinking of that path and practicing that dharma, within whatever is thereby attained, the spirit follows the thought and enters in directly. Through this, one comes to realize a spirit's own dharma-gate, the spirit lending it its own power — bringing forth, at times, deep deviant concentrations, and eloquence and apparent wisdom, knowledge of fortune and misfortune in the world, strange and marvelous spiritual powers, manifesting rare and wondrous feats that move sentient beings, spreading deviant transformation widely; at times committing great evil and destroying others' wholesome roots, or, though outwardly doing good, acting in a manner mixed through with falsehood.

zh: 世人無智，但見異人，謂是賢聖，深心信伏。然其內心顛倒，專行鬼法，常以鬼法教人，故信行之者，則破正戒，破正見，破威儀，破淨命。或時噉食糞穢，裸形無恥，不敬三尊、父母、師長；或毀壞經書、形像、塔寺，作諸逆罪，斷滅善根，現平等相；或自讚說所行平等，故於非道無障無礙，毀他修善，云非正道；或說無因無果，或說邪因邪果。如是邪說紛然，壞亂正法，其有聞受之者，邪法染心，既內證邪禪、三昧、智斷、功德種種法門，外則辯才無盡，威風化物，故得名聞、眷屬、供養、禮敬、稱歎等利，是以《九十六種道經》云：人為說法，鬼神加力，則一切聞者無不信受，一切見者咸生愛敬。以有如斯等事故，深心執著，不可迴轉，邪行顛倒，種種非一。若如是者，當知是人遠離聖法，身壞命終，墮三惡道中，是事如《大品經》及《摩訶衍論》中廣說。若欲知鬼神之相，當尋《九十六種道經》，細心比類分別，事則可知。
en: People of the world, lacking wisdom, seeing only someone extraordinary, take them to be a sage or a noble one, and believe in and submit to them with a deeply devoted mind. Yet inwardly, such a person's mind is inverted, devoted single-mindedly to spirit-practices, and constantly teaching others through spirit-practices — so that those who believe and follow them come to break the correct precepts, break right view, break proper conduct, and break the purity of their livelihood. At times they devour filth and excrement, go about naked and shameless, showing no reverence toward the Triple Gem, their parents, or their teachers; or they destroy sūtra texts, images, stūpas, and temples, committing every manner of grave offense, cutting off wholesome roots entirely, all while displaying a mark of equality; or they praise themselves, proclaiming that what they do is equality, so that in following what is not the path they see no hindrance or obstruction whatsoever, while disparaging others who cultivate what is truly wholesome, calling it not the correct path at all; or they teach that there is no cause and no effect, or teach a deviant cause and a deviant effect.

Such deviant teachings as these run rampant, corrupting and disordering the true Dharma; and whoever hears and accepts them has their mind stained by this deviant dharma — inwardly coming to realize deviant dhyāna, samādhi, wisdom and severance, merit, and various such dharma-gates, while outwardly possessing inexhaustible eloquence, an awe-inspiring manner that sways others; and so such a person gains fame, followers, offerings, veneration, praise, and other such benefits. Hence the Sūtra of the Ninety-Six Paths says: when such a person expounds the teaching, spirits lend their power, so that everyone who hears it cannot help but believe and accept it, and everyone who sees it cannot help but come to love and revere it. Because of such matters as these, one's attachment grows deeply fixed and cannot be turned back, and deviant, inverted conduct proliferates in every manner, not of one kind only. If this is how it is, one should know that such a person has become far removed from the noble Dharma, and, when body and life come to an end, falls into the three lower destinies — this matter is explained in full in the Larger Sūtra and in the Mahāyāna treatise. If one wishes to know the marks of spirits, one should search the Sūtra of the Ninety-Six Paths, and, examining it carefully, distinguish like from like — the matter can then be understood.

zh: 問曰：邪法相應行惡之者，現在之過，如是命終，當生三惡道中。其有偽心行善之者，現在之失，云何命終復生何處？答曰：此人身、口行善，雖似佛法，而解心邪僻，若不覺知，障發三乘無漏，雖不會真，於顛倒心中，或時亦能興顯三寶，勸物修善。是人命終未必墮於地獄、畜生、餓鬼之中，而隨所與鬼神相應之法，共彼鬼神同生一處，還為彼眷屬。或時得生人天之中，故《九十六種道經》中說，上有六十餘道，邪倒罪障重故，悉須說呪治之；下有二十餘道，邪惑罪障小輕，直覺知而已。
en: Question: for someone who corresponds to a deviant dharma and does evil, the fault is plain in this present life, and, when life ends in this way, they will be born into the three lower destinies. But for someone whose mind is false while outwardly doing good, what is the fault in this present life, and where, then, are they reborn when life ends? Answer: such a person's body and speech act wholesomely, and although this resembles the Buddhadharma, their understanding and mind are deviant; if they fail to recognize this, it obstructs the arising of the three vehicles' uncontaminated attainment. Although they never truly encounter the truth, within their own inverted mind they may, at times, still be able to promote and display the Triple Gem, and urge others toward wholesome cultivation. When such a person's life ends, they will not necessarily fall into hell, into the animal realm, or among the hungry ghosts, but instead, following whichever spirit-dharma they corresponded to, will be born together with that same spirit in one place, becoming, in turn, one of its own followers. At times they may even be born among humans or gods. Hence the Sūtra of the Ninety-Six Paths says that, of these paths, more than sixty of the higher kind, being weighed down with deviance and grave offense, all require incantations to treat them; while more than twenty of the lower kind, their deviant confusion and offense being slight, require only recognition alone.

zh: 復次，是人雖生天人之中，而冥密常係屬魔邪之道，樂近邪師，樂聞邪法，樂行邪道，供養、親近、稱揚、讚歎修邪行者，見有正學三乘之人，不樂親近，或生惱亂，故《法華經》云：「若魔、若魔子、若魔女、若魔民，若為魔所著者。」《大品經》亦云：「若魔天、若魔人。」故知是人雖生人天之中，猶係屬於魔，常起魔業，乃至雖得出家，猶造魔業。故《涅槃經》云：「佛去世後五百歲中，魔道漸興，魔作比丘，壞亂佛法。」亦如《大集經》中廣辯魔業之相，是中應廣分別。
en: Furthermore: even though such a person is born among gods or humans, they remain secretly and constantly bound to the way of demons and deviance — delighting in drawing near to deviant teachers, delighting in hearing deviant teachings, delighting in practicing deviant paths, making offerings to, drawing close to, praising, and extolling those who cultivate deviant conduct; while, upon meeting those who rightly study the three vehicles, they take no delight in drawing near, and may even grow disturbed and hostile. Hence the Lotus Sūtra says: "Whether a demon, a demon's son, a demon's daughter, a demon's subject, or one possessed by a demon." The Larger Sūtra likewise says: "Whether a demon among the gods, or a demon among humans." Hence it is known that although such a person is born among humans or gods, they remain bound to demons, constantly giving rise to demonic karma — and even should they obtain ordination, they still create demonic karma. Hence the Nirvāṇa Sūtra says: "In the five hundred years after the Buddha has passed from the world, the way of demons will gradually flourish; demons will become monks, and corrupt and disorder the Buddhadharma." This, too, is discussed at length in the Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra's own broad treatment of the marks of demonic karma, which should be distinguished at length here.

zh: 如一動觸中邪相如是，餘七觸中亦具有此邪相，應當別知。如根本禪邪相如是，餘十四門禪及諸禪中若事若理，皆有邪偽之法，其事云云，非可具說。問曰：發邪觸時，為當具發如上所說二十邪事，為當不具？答曰：或具或不具無在。若觸發時，但有一邪法，不即除之，便墮邪定，何況具足二十邪法。所以者何？譬如二十人共行，若一是賊，則誤十九人。禪中亦爾，有一惡法，破壞諸善，不名正定，況復多耶？略辯一觸相如是，則餘七觸邪相亦然。復次，更有異禪門邪法入定中，亦應識知，所謂餘禪門境界邪法，如一不淨觀禪入此定中，亦有二十邪法來入此定，餘十四門禪亦當如是一一分別，是中應廣說。行者若脫證此法，須善識知，方便照了，不著邪定之法，即自便謝。
en: Just as the deviant marks within this single tactile sensation of movement are as described, the remaining seven tactile sensations likewise possess these same deviant marks in full, and should be distinguished individually. And just as the deviant marks within the root dhyānas are as described, the remaining fourteen gates of dhyāna, and every dhyāna's phenomenal conduct and underlying principle alike, all have their own deviant and false dharmas — the matter is manifold, and cannot be described in full.

Question: when a deviant tactile sensation arises, must all twenty deviant matters given above arise together in full, or need they not be complete? Answer: whether complete or incomplete makes no difference either way. If, when the sensation arises, even a single deviant dharma is present and is not removed at once, one falls into a deviant concentration regardless — how much more so if all twenty deviant dharmas are present together? Why is this? It is like twenty people traveling together: if even one among them is a thief, all nineteen others are led astray. Within dhyāna it is exactly the same — a single unwholesome dharma is enough to break every wholesome quality apart, and cannot be called right concentration at all, let alone when many such dharmas are present. This, in brief, distinguishes the marks within a single tactile sensation; the deviant marks within the remaining seven sensations follow the same pattern.

Furthermore: there are, besides this, deviant dharmas from other dhyāna-gates that may enter into this same concentration, and these too should be recognized — that is, the deviant dharmas belonging to the states of other dhyāna-gates. For instance, when the contemplation of impurity itself enters into this same concentration, its own twenty deviant dharmas may likewise enter along with it; and the remaining fourteen gates of dhyāna should each be distinguished individually in the same way — this should be explained at length here. Should the practitioner happen to realize such a dharma, one must skillfully recognize it, illuminating it through skillful means, and, by not clinging to this deviant, concentrated dharma, it will of itself simply pass away.

The ten pairs give the treatise's most granular diagnostic scheme yet — every wholesome-looking mark of concentration has a twin that is either too much or too little of the same thing (excess versus deficiency in the sensation itself, concentration versus agitation, sorrow versus joy, bondage versus a supposed liberation that breeds overweening pride), which is what makes them genuinely hard to catch: each deviant mark isn't the opposite of a good sign but an excess or shortfall of it. The escalation from personal danger (madness, self-harm) to social danger (a false teacher whose spirit-lent charisma draws devoted followers into the same deviance) to cosmic danger (being reborn bound to that same spirit-realm, echoing the *Lotus Sūtra*'s and *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*'s warnings about demons operating from inside the monastic robe) reads as a warning against exactly the kind of uncritical veneration the treatise elsewhere insists a genuine teacher must be able to withstand.

quiz.q: In the deviant marks of mark-verification, how many pairs are given for a single tactile sensation, and how are they distinguished?
options: ten pairs, each distinguished as excess or insufficiency
eight pairs, by the eight sensations
five pairs, by good and evil
quiz.why: "With reference to a single tactile sensation, ten pairs of deviant dharmas are given in brief ... These ten pairs, clarifying the deviant marks, are each distinguished in terms of excess on the one hand or insufficiency on the other." Ten pairs make twenty unwholesome sensations.

quiz.q: In the ninth pair, bondage and liberation, what is the "liberation" mark?
options: one supposes oneself to have realized emptiness or signlessness and attained the fruit, giving rise to overweening pride
quiz.why: "As for liberation: when the sensation arises, one supposes oneself to have realized the concentration of emptiness or signlessness, to have attained the path and its fruit, severed the fetters, and become liberated — giving rise to overweening pride." The hindrances covering the mind is "bondage," and not seeing the body is "emptiness."

quiz.q: In the pair "mind too rigid or too soft," what similes are used?
options: wood and stone; a dark room
rigid: like tile or stone, hard to turn; soft: like soft mud, unfit to be a vessel
quiz.why: "As for rigidity, when the sensation arises, the mind becomes hard and unyielding ... just like a tile or a stone, difficult to turn or change ... As for softness ... just like soft mud, unfit to be shaped into any vessel." Wood and stone describe "existence," and the dark room "darkness."

quiz.q: If a deviant dharma corresponds to a spirit-practice of the ninety-six paths and goes unrecognized, what happens?
options: the spirit enters with the thought and lends its power: deep deviant concentrations, eloquence, fortune-telling, marvels, spreading deviant transformation
quiz.why: "Within whatever is thereby attained, the spirit follows the thought and enters in directly. Through this, one comes to realize a spirit's own dharma-gate, the spirit lending it its own power — bringing forth, at times, deep deviant concentrations ... knowledge of fortune and misfortune in the world, strange and marvelous spiritual powers."

quiz.q: Where is one reborn who does good with a false mind, corresponding to a spirit-practice?
options: not necessarily the lower destinies; born together with that spirit as its follower, or among humans and gods while still secretly bound to Māra's way
quiz.why: "When such a person's life ends, they will not necessarily fall into hell, into the animal realm, or among the hungry ghosts, but instead, following whichever spirit-dharma they corresponded to, will be born together with that same spirit in one place, becoming, in turn, one of its own followers. At times they may even be born among humans or gods."

quiz.q: If only one deviant dharma is present when a sensation arises, does one still fall into deviant concentration? What simile is used?
options: yes; like gold in a foul sack
yes; like twenty people traveling together, if one is a thief, the other nineteen are led astray
quiz.why: "If, when the sensation arises, even a single deviant dharma is present and is not removed at once, one falls into a deviant concentration regardless ... It is like twenty people traveling together: if even one among them is a thief, all nineteen others are led astray."
